title: Gérard Depardieu Withdraws Sexual Assault Appeal, Apologizing to Victims
summary: The French actor admitted guilt on the morning his appeal trial was to begin in Paris, accepting his conviction for groping two women on a film set.

The French movie star Gérard Depardieu withdrew his appeal on Monday against a sexual-assault conviction, admitting his guilt and offering his apologies to two women he groped while working on set with them in 2021.


The announcement, released by Mr. Depardieu’s new lawyer, came on the morning that the appeal trial had been scheduled to start in Paris.


A prolific actor who was once one of France’s most popular leading men, Mr. Depardieu, 77, was[convicted last year](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/13/world/europe/gerard-depardieu-guilty-sexual-assault-trial.html) of sexually assaulting the women, one a set decorator and the other an assistant director, on the set of the film “Les Volets Verts.” He received a suspended sentence of 18 months and the judge ordered that his name be added to France’s sex offender registry.


The ruling was considered a landmark win for French women in the post #MeToo world.


Throughout the four-day trial last year, the actor denied sexually assaulting anyone, and his lawyer called the two victims liars — earning a rare ruling of “secondary victimization” by the judge.


But in a statement released on Monday by his new lawyer, David-Olivier Kaminski, Mr. Depardieu said he accepted the verdict and offered his “deep and sincere apologies.”


“I never, ever intended to hurt the women I encountered. But I have come to understand that intent changes nothing about the wound,” Mr. Depardieu said.
